summary: Implemented GET /api/v1/signing-sessions/{sessionId}, POST .../otp/verify, POST .../otp/resend, POST .../sign, and POST .../decline on top of the sibling T-CONTRACTS-API/T-SIGNERS-API task's `signers`/`contracts` tables (no new table or migration -- this task owns no table per context.json). New files: app/schemas/signing_session.py (SigningSessionResponse, VerifyOtpRequest, VerifyOtpResponse, ApplySignatureRequest, ApplySignatureResponse, DeclineSignatureRequest, DeclineSignatureResponse -- field-for-field per context.json), app/repositories/signing_sessions.py (signer-by-id / contract-by-id lookups, kept separate from the sibling task's app/repositories/signers.py per CLAUDE.md's module-addition rule), app/services/signing_sessions.py (all business rules), app/routers/signing_sessions.py, wired into app/main.py. Behavior implemented: a signing 'session' is simply the owning Signer row (sessionId == signer id) since context.json defines no signing_sessions table and the Signer's link is the SIGNER role's only credential; sequential eligibility (UC7-BR-001) checked by Signing Order alone; the document viewer/Signature Pad stay hidden until OTP verification (UC7-BR-003/016); a 6-digit-numeric OTP format check (UC7-FV-002) with per-attempt tracking, a 15-minute lockout after the third consecutive invalid OTP that leaves Signer Status unchanged (UC7-AF-001); lazy link-expiry-to-Expired transition evaluated on every touch, since this sandbox has no scheduler (UC7-BR-020), with resend available to SIGNER or the owning CONTRACT_OWNER to re-issue a fresh OTP/link and revert to Sent; applying a signature requires OTP-verified + Viewed + all-prior-signed, records signatureData/signatureType/ip/timestamp, advances the next signer in order to Sent, and auto-transitions the contract to Executed only once every signer is Signed (UC7-BR-004/007/017/019); declining requires Viewed status and a non-blank reason, sets the signer Declined and the contract to 'SignatureDeclined', halting all subsequent signers' access (UC7-AF-002, UC7-BR-008/018); contract-wide 'SignatureDeclined' state blocks every other signer's GET/verify/sign/decline (UC7-BR-014's 'no access unless an eligible Signer' is covered by `require_roles('SIGNER')` doing the role gate, combined with this per-signer eligibility). Added tests/test_signing_sessions.py (23 new tests) covering the role/auth matrix, sequencing, OTP validation/lockout, resend eligibility and ownership, signing + auto-advance + auto-Executed, and decline halting routing. `python -m compileall app` passed; `pytest -q` passed (280 passed, including this task's 23 new tests). No live Postgres is reachable in this sandbox (the same constraint every prior task output on this branch recorded), so the curl-against-a-booted-uvicorn verification step was substituted with an in-process FastAPI TestClient exercising the real app against a sqlite-backed session: 401 missing-role, 403 wrong-role, 404 unknown session, 200 GET happy path, 400 malformed OTP, 200 OTP-verify success revealing the document/Signature Pad, 400 blank Signature Pad, 200 sign success auto-transitioning the contract to Executed on the final signer, 409 resend/decline once already Signed -- every response body was diffed field-by-field against context.json's DTOs. Confirmed all 5 routes appear in app.openapi()['paths'] with the right methods, and that both X-User-Role/X-User-Id security schemes are declared on them.

pr.title: Implement signing-sessions endpoints (UC7 e-signature)
pr.body: Implements GET /api/v1/signing-sessions/{sessionId} and its otp/verify, otp/resend, sign, decline sub-actions per the UC6-UC7-combined module contract. See task output for full details and judgement calls.

blockers: No `signing_sessions` table exists in context.json (this task's 'Tables you may read' is empty) and no table in the foundation/sibling tasks' schema represents a distinct 'session' concept. Treated `sessionId` as the owning Signer row's id -- the Signer's emailed link/OTP is the SIGNER role's only credential, functioning like a session token. Recorded per TASK.md's 'A missing table' guidance; no new table or migration was added.

The SIGNER role has no row in `users` (external signers are recorded only on the `signers` table by name/email), so these endpoints do not use `current_tenant_id` (which requires resolving X-User-Id against `users` and would 401 every external signer). Access is instead scoped entirely by the caller knowing `sessionId`; the CONTRACT_OWNER-only branch of resend additionally checks `contract.contract_owner_id == X-User-Id`. `created_by`/`updated_by` writes fall back to the signer's own id when X-User-Id isn't a UUID resolvable to a real actor (these columns are plain NOT NULL uuid with no FK, per app/models/mixins.py, so this never violates a constraint). This is a deliberate deviation from the tenant-scoped pattern every other resource in this module uses, since no sibling task defines how an external, accountless signer's identity maps to this contract's auth model.

`contractStatus`/`signerStatus` enum literals written are the exact strings context.json's DTOs enumerate (`Sent`, `Executed`, `SignatureDeclined`, `Viewed`, `Signed`, `Declined`, `Expired`) -- compact, no spaces -- matching the compound-word convention the sibling T-CONTRACTS-API signers service already established for contract.status values outside its own enum (`SignatureConnectionFailed`), even though the stories themselves spell it 'Signature Declined' with a space and 'Ready for Signature' with spaces for the pre-send precondition. Followed the DTO's literal spelling, not the story prose, per TASK.md's 'Contract fidelity is a hard requirement'.

GET returns 404 for a Signer whose status is still 'Pending' (added to signers but never sent a link) -- the response DTO's signerStatus enum has no slot for 'Pending' and there is no active session to describe yet. Treated as 'session not found' rather than inventing a sixth enum value or a distinct blocked-access response shape.

When an OTP-locked or link-expired session is touched again (GET/verify/sign/decline), the response is a 403 Forbidden (one shared error body), not a 200 carrying the VerifyOtpResponse's `lockedUntil`/`errorMessage` fields -- those fields are populated only by the specific `otp/verify` call that creates or extends the lockout, following the existing lifecycle_negotiation module's identical Locked/Expired precedent in this codebase.

MF-001's 'records their name, email, IP address and timestamp' on sign is satisfied by reading `request.client.host` in the router and passing it to the service -- there is no authenticated session/proxy layer in this header-auth stub that verifies a client IP, so this is best-effort and will read a test-client or proxy address rather than a real end-user IP in any deployment behind a reverse proxy.

MF-001/BR-019's audit-certificate generation on the final signature is NOT performed by this task: that behavior (and the `audit_certificates` row) belongs to the sibling T-CONTRACTS-API signers service, which already lazily materializes the certificate on first GET of `/contracts/{contractId}/audit-certificate` once `contract.status == 'Executed'` (see that task's own blockers). This task only flips `contract.status` to 'Executed'; no certificate file or emails are generated here, since no SMTP/document-generation dependency is declared in this repo's manifest (CLAUDE.md permits only already-declared dependencies).

TASK.md's verification steps reference `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`/`dotnet run`, which contradict this repo's actual Python/FastAPI stack per CLAUDE.md and the existing codebase -- ran `python -m compileall app`, `pytest -q`, and an in-process FastAPI TestClient-based smoke exercise instead, per CLAUDE.md's authority on HOW to build.

No live Postgres instance is reachable in this sandbox, so the curl-against-a-booted-uvicorn-server verification step was substituted with an in-process FastAPI TestClient against the real app plus a sqlite-backed session and `app.openapi()`, matching the substitution every prior task's output on this branch already recorded.

This is a re-run per the human reviewer's 're run' feedback; no prior output file (`.api-gen/outputs/T-SIGNING-SESSIONS-API.json`) or any signing-session router/service/repository/schema/test code existed anywhere on this branch to revise -- only the sibling foundation/contracts/signers tasks' models, migrations and their own router/service code were already present. This run is therefore the first implementation of these five endpoints, built fresh rather than edited from a prior attempt.

Marked `status` as PARTIAL rather than SUCCESS because of the judgement calls above (no dedicated session table, no tenant-scoped auth, best-effort IP capture) that a reviewer should confirm against the rest of the UC7 module as it continues to be built out, even though every endpoint in this task's `endpoints` list is implemented, tested, and passes its own verification.
